body:
_Migrated from issue #1323, filed 2026-08-03._

Split out of the #1321 cross-family review rather than widened into it — this is a pre-existing hazard the #1318 work did not introduce and does not close.

## What

Both bookmark write routes begin with a bulk delete, before anything that guards a database failure:

- `cps/web.py` `set_bookmark` — `ub.session.query(ub.Bookmark).filter(...).delete()`
- `cps/api/reader.py` `save_bookmark` — same

`Query.delete()` issues SQL immediately. Under contention it can raise `OperationalError` right there, outside both `ub.session_flush()` and `ub.session_commit()`, so neither helper's rollback runs.

`ub.session` is a single concrete session created once by `ub.init_db()` and shared across requests. There is no app teardown that rolls it back. So a failure raised by that delete leaves the shared session in a failed state, and the next request to touch it gets `InvalidRequestError` until some other code path happens to roll back.

## Why it matters

#1318 made these routes honest about a write that did not land, but only for failures raised *inside* the two helpers. A lock hit by the opening delete produces a 500 from the unhandled exception — which is at least not a false success — and then a session that can poison unrelated requests.

## Shape of the fix

Probably not per-route try/except; the general answer is a teardown that rolls back the shared session when a request ends with an exception (`app.teardown_request` / `teardown_appcontext`), so no single failure can strand it. Worth checking whether any other route has the same open-with-immediate-SQL shape.

Found by the Terra review pass on #1321 (finding E); confirmed by reading `ub.init_db` and the two routes.
title: Bookmark routes can raise before any commit guard, leaving the shared session failed
